key_insight: Electrode lattice vibrations can tune competing phases in ultrathin BiFeO₃ nanocapacitors independently of conventional strain and electrostatic controls.
engineering_relevance: Interfacial phonon bias offers a design lever for ferroelectric nanodevices, rather than a demonstrated advance in solar cells.
method: Use first-principles-accurate machine-learned interatomic potentials and molecular dynamics.
Model symmetric BiFeO₃ nanocapacitors with metallic perovskite-oxide electrodes.
Vary electrode octahedral-tilt orientation and amplitude while holding elastic and electric boundary conditions fixed.
evidence_signal: Simulations show altered phase stability, shifts in the ferroelectric transition temperature, and antiferroelectric-like switching at ambient conditions; the abstract provides no numerical effect sizes.
watch_item: Experimental validation is needed to establish whether electrode tilt landscapes can be independently controlled in fabricated devices.
paper_title: Engineering ferroelectric nanocapacitors through interfacial phonon bias
